epistle noun

classical

epistula, epistulae f.

noun, first declension

a letter; an epistle

Any letter; in church the reading from the letters of the apostles. The Vulgate spells it epistola.

Other words

  • apostolus, apostolī m. — the Apostle: Paul’s letters, the epistle reading

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Aug. Conf. 8.12.29: cōdicem apostolī

    In the Fathers “the apostle” is Paul, and his letters; the Orthodox still call the book of the Epistles and its reading “the Apostle”.

Examples

  • 1epistola: short i (Lewis & Short ĕpīstŏla, taking the heavy syllable for a long vowel). Greek ἐπιστολή, from ἐπί, with short ι; Lewis & Short’s main entry, ĕpistŭla, leaves the i unmarked.

    Et cum lēcta fuerit apud vōs epistola haec, facite ut et in Lāodicēnsium ecclēsiā legātur1

    And when this letter has been read among you, see that it is read in the church of the Laodiceans tooVulg. Col. 4.16

  • ibi enim posueram cōdicem apostolī cum inde surrēxeram. arripuī, aperuī, et lēgī in silentiō

    for I had left the book of the Apostle there when I got up. I snatched it up, opened it, and read in silenceAug. Conf. 8.12.29

See also Bible, Gospel, apostle.
